newsitem.title: JAPAN: Jpn long-term rates too low-ex-MOF official quoted.
newsitem.headline: Jpn long-term rates too low-ex-MOF official quoted.

text.p: Makoto Utsumi, a former Japanese vice finance minister for international affairs, said that current long-term interest rates are too low and reflect excessive pessimism about the outlook for the Japanese economy, a foreign wire service reported on Wednesday.

The report quoted Utsumi, who is now a professor at Keio University, as saying in an interview that current Japanese long-term interest rates of below three percent reflect a "too pessimistic" view of the Japanese economy as they assume economic growth of below two percent.

Utsumi was also quoted as saying the Bank of Japan will have a difficult time raising interest rates until a recovery in the economy can be confirmed. He declined to elaborate further, the report said.
